beats.narration_text: This is Liam, narrating for Deepa. My Week 6 Humanitarians AI volunteer work combined learning Brutalist Film-as-Code with supporting Sanjana Rao’s YouTube team. I followed Sanjana’s workflow for reviewing submissions, preparing metadata, and uploading videos for further review. This update covers that team contribution alongside my STEM and progress video production.

beats.narration_text: The first video was Energy Recycling in Photonics — Three Things Called Recycling. It distinguished reusing pump light, reusing photons, and recovering waste heat. Those are different meanings of recycling in photonic hardware. My review and metadata preparation needed to represent that distinction clearly, rather than treat the three ideas as interchangeable.

beats.narration_text: The second video was The Denominator Problem: When Percentages Mislead. It used a Snickerdoodle recipe-checking investigation involving ninety-seven recipes, six hundred sixteen findings, and missing scripts. Its lesson was that percentages depend on what is being counted. These figures describe the submitted video’s example, not a separate investigation I carried out.

I informed Sanjana that they were uploaded. I learned to keep my review outcome, the upload-for-review step, and final approval or publication separate.

beats.narration_text: The videos were prepared in landscape sixteen by nine and separately reflowed portrait nine by sixteen. I learned that matching the required dimensions is only the starting point. Each format needs checks for typography, safe areas, scene timing, audio audibility, and narration synchronization. A portrait composition needs its own readable layout, not a crop.

beats.narration_text: The production logs record text overflow, small type in final-resolution frames, and portrait branding too low for the safe area. The fixes included larger type, shorter portrait labels, adjusted spacing, and rerendering affected scenes. That taught me to inspect the actual exports, document failures and corrections, and distinguish automated checks from human review.
